feature: Settings: Change control policy + Departments persistence (Git #1592). Backend only -- no `Design/portal/` export exists yet for the Settings page (artifacts/portal has no page to wire), so this manifest is apiTests-only against artifacts/api-server/src/routes/portal-settings-change-control.ts and portal-settings-departments.ts. Both sections were 100% client-only React state before this (#1463's pv2-set-cc-nodata / pv2-set-dept-nodata badges) -- these tests prove the real endpoints persist per tenant.
notes: MUTATES THE SHARED TESTBED TENANT'S REAL SETTINGS. CC-CLEANUP-* and DEPT-CLEANUP-* at the end of this file revert the policy to disabled/empty-approvers and delete the synthetic department mapping this run creates, so no run leaves the shared tenant in a changed state for the next one.

APPROVERS ARE VALIDATED AGAINST REAL ACTIVE USERS OF THIS TENANT, NOT ARBITRARY STRINGS. CC-APPROVERS-SETUP extracts a real wire person id (portal-ownership.ts's own personIdForUser format, 'u{id}') from GET /api/portal/ownership so CC-APPROVERS-OK exercises the real fail-closed validation path rather than a fixture id that happens to look right.

DEPARTMENTS: THE TEST DEPARTMENT NAME IS SYNTHETIC ON PURPOSE. This DB's real testbed users currently carry no `department` attribute value (verified directly against local Postgres), so there is no real department name to map without inventing test data on top of a real user. Mapping a department NAME the tenant has never had a member in is itself a real, honest state the route supports (a customer can map a department by group before anyone is in it) -- DEPT-MAP-OK asserts exactly that (n: 0, src: 'group').

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED account; extract the bearer.
CC1 -- GET change-control serves a real payload shape even before this tenant has ever saved anything (honest defaults, not a 404).
CC2 -- the full notification-rule event catalogue is always present, defaulted or saved.
CC3 -- save the policy: turn it on, gate 'fix', require 2 signatures.
CC4 -- IT PERSISTED: a fresh GET reflects the saved policy, not the request that just ran.
CC5 -- ...and the gate is really keyed, not just accepted and dropped.
CC-APPROVERS-SETUP -- a real active person id off this tenant's own Ownership matrix, so the approvers write below exercises real fail-closed validation.
CC-APPROVERS-BAD -- a personId that names no active user of this tenant is REJECTED, not silently accepted (fail closed, matching the ownership overlay's own convention).
CC-APPROVERS-OK -- a real personId for this tenant is accepted.
CC-APPROVERS-PERSISTED -- the saved approver reads back from a fresh GET.
CC-NOTIF-OK -- one notification rule saved by its real event key.
CC-NOTIF-BADKEY -- an unknown event key is rejected rather than silently stored under a key nothing else reads.
CC-CLEANUP-POLICY -- revert the policy to disabled/default so this shared tenant is not left changed for the next run.
CC-CLEANUP-APPROVERS -- clear the band back to empty.
DEPT1 -- GET departments serves live headcounts + the mapping overlay in one payload.
DEPT-MAP-BADREQUEST -- mapping by group with no securityGroupId is rejected rather than silently stored as a group mapping to nothing.
DEPT-MAP-OK -- map a department to a security group.
DEPT-MAP-PERSISTED -- the mapping reads back from a fresh GET, with its real (zero) live headcount alongside it.
DEPT-CLEANUP -- clear the synthetic mapping so this shared tenant is not left changed for the next run.
